title: Why Lions Are Scared of Giraffes

sources.kick: National Geographic 2019 (San Diego Zoo researcher: an adult male giraffe can kill a lion easily with one kick)
sources.drinking: Giraffe Conservation Foundation; Smithsonian: giraffes scout for upwards of an hour before drinking
sources.zebras: Science News 2024 / BMC Biology 2025: collar-camera zebras spend ~2x longer and synchronise movement with giraffes, likely using them as sentinels
sources.speed: giraffes can run up to ~60 km/h
sources.calves: Bristol / Mongabay 2018: lions target young giraffes; Serengeti ~60% of calves die in their first year

sentences.text: Lions are scared of an animal that can't climb, can't hide, and nearly dies every time it drinks.
To drink, a giraffe has to do the splits, so it checks for lions for up to an hour first.
But at nearly six metres tall, it's the best lookout on the savanna.
Zebras even follow giraffes around, just to use them as an alarm.
If a lion gets close, it can sprint at sixty kilometres an hour.
One kick from an adult giraffe can kill a lion.
